drivers: Recovery balance not reported (missing in dataset), ACWR cannot be calculated (acute/chronic load metrics absent), resting HR trend unavailable (no baseline or recent values provided), HRV and sleep metrics missing entirely, training readiness not included in data
readiness.guidance: Without objective recovery metrics, training must prioritize sustainability and avoid intensity spikes — assume neutral readiness and monitor response to low-stress efforts.

monthly_review.summary: Pace improved sharply this month while volume increased modestly; aerobic TE rose slightly but cadence dropped from last month’s peak, suggesting a possible trade-off between speed and neuromuscular efficiency.
monthly_review.highlight: The 28-second-per-kilometer pace improvement (from 8:54 to 8:26) is the most notable finding — and it coincides with a +6 bpm rise in average HR and worsening Running Economy (+0.47 ml/kg/km), indicating effort cost increased despite faster pace, consistent with a shift toward higher-intensity work seen in zone distribution (Z3 rose from 26% to 31%, Z4 from 8% to 21%).

goal_tracker.message: The runner has already exceeded last month’s distance (56.4 vs 51.3 km) and run count (11 vs 10) with 9 days remaining — no additional sessions or km are needed to match last month. Given missing recovery data and signs of elevated physiological cost (higher HR, worse efficiency), chasing further volume or intensity would be inadvisable.

insights.title: Zone 3–4 dominance replaced easy running
insights.body: Z1 dropped from 43% in August to 21% in September, while Z3+Z4 rose from 34% to 52% — a major shift away from true recovery/easy effort, aligning with the 6 bpm HR increase and reduced cadence (149 → 144 spm).

insights.title: Faster pace came at clear aerobic cost
insights.body: Despite best pace improving from 7:33 (453 sec/km) in August to 6:09 (369 sec/km) in September, Running Economy worsened from 14.12 to 14.59 ml/kg/km — meaning each km now costs ~0.5 ml more O₂, likely due to increased Z3/Z4 reliance and reduced Z1 volume.

insights.title: Cadence decline correlates with ground contact increase
insights.body: Cadence fell from 149 spm (Aug) to 144 spm (Sep), and recent runs show rising ground contact time (e.g., 327 ms on 9/6 long run vs median ~305 ms in recent easy runs), suggesting fatigue or compromised stride elasticity under higher loads.

recommendations.action: Replace one midweek run with 45 min Zone 1 walk or non-weight-bearing cross-training (e.g., cycling at HR <115 bpm)
recommendations.reason: Z1 volume collapsed to 21% — below the minimum 30% needed for autonomic recovery and capillary development; this restores foundational aerobic stimulus without cardiac or musculoskeletal stress.

recommendations.action: Perform two 10-min barefoot strides on grass post-run (Tuesday & Thursday), focusing on light footstrike and cadence ≥160 spm
recommendations.reason: Cadence dropped 5 spm while vertical oscill remained stable (~8.2 mm avg) — indicating potential overstriding; neuromuscular retraining can improve stride efficiency without added load.

recommendations.action: Hold all runs at HR ≤135 bpm for next 5 days — use real-time HR alert and pause if exceeded for >30 sec
recommendations.reason: Average HR rose +6 bpm while efficiency declined — enforcing strict HR ceiling prevents further decoupling and reinforces aerobic pacing discipline.

risk_flags.evidence: Aerobic TE rose from 2.6% (Aug) to 2.9% (Sep); recent long run (9/6) showed 5.0% TE at 12:22 min/km pace — above 5% threshold indicating cardiovascular drift
risk_flags.action: Remove all Z4+ efforts until aerobic TE stabilizes ≤2.5% across three consecutive easy runs

risk_flags.evidence: Cadence dropped 5 spm while ground contact time increased in longest run (327 ms vs typical 292–309 ms), and stride length decreased from 83–84 cm to 77 cm during slow long run — classic sign of late-run neuromuscular fatigue
risk_flags.action: Insert 2x weekly mobility drills targeting hip flexor and calf elasticity before any run

weekly_focus.description: Re-establish Z1 as the dominant stimulus to lower autonomic strain, improve oxygen utilization efficiency, and rebuild neuromuscular coordination — using heart rate as the sole governor, not pace.
suggested_sessions: 5 km easy run (HR ≤135 bpm, cadence ≥150 spm)
Strides + mobility (10 min barefoot strides + 10 min dynamic calf/hip flexor work)
